description: Sprint 3 Lever Catalog — 4 transit-service levers for the simulation engine (v1)
design_rationale: Simulator v1 exposes only transit-service parameters that a transit agency can directly control. Headway features (headway_peak_am_min, headway_early_min) are physically inverse of frequency (headway = 60/freq) and are auto-derived inside simulator.py — not user-facing — to prevent impossible states. Demographic variables (poverty_rate_pct, hh_no_vehicle_pct) are forecast outputs from ACS TimeSeries, not policy levers; they flow into projected_need_2027 as fixed baseline inputs. Need-side stress-test scenarios (e.g., poverty +5pp) are a candidate v2 feature — see Sprint 3/future/ for preserved OLS coefficients.

levers.notes: Peak AM frequency. SHAP #1 driver. Higher frequency -> lower deficit. Simulator must also update headway_peak_am_min = 60 / (current + delta) and clamp both to data_range.
Early morning frequency. SHAP #3 driver. Low baseline (mean ~3 tph). Simulator must also update headway_early_min and clamp.
Weekend service as fraction of weekday. SHAP #2 driver. Most tracts at ~0.43. Target-based scenarios (e.g., set to 0.80) are more intuitive than delta-based.

Rail mode share. Not in SHAP top 6 but what-if analysis shows it is the single most impactful lever: +10pp -> -0.0149 deficit, 98% of tracts improve. Very low baseline (mean 1.1%). Increase = modal shift to rail.

non_adjustable_features.reason: Auto-derived from freq_peak_am_tph (headway = 60/freq). Updated internally by simulator.
Auto-derived from freq_early_tph. Updated internally by simulator.
Spatial context — depends on neighboring tracts, not a single-tract lever.
Spatial context — depends on neighboring tracts.
ACS temporal trend slope — historical, not adjustable.

future_v2_features.need_side_stress_tests: Demographic shock scenarios (poverty +Xpp, no-vehicle +Ypp) adjusting projected_need_2027 via Sprint 2a formula weights. OLS coefficients preserved in Sprint 3/future/Sprint3_Need_OLS_Coefficients.json.
future_v2_features.spatial_spillover: Adjusting neighbor_mean_* features to model corridor-wide improvements.
